hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge into the output with a 3x3 conv adds a whole learnable path, a much larger gain than replacing another op.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a conv gives a bigger gain than swapping one op for another.
Adding a conv on a previously empty input-to-output edge gives a large gain compared with replacing an existing op.
Activating the first edge, which was cut, opens the deeper paths through node 1 and so gains more than a swap.
Removing a conv edge into the output costs far more accuracy than removing a pooling or skip edge.
Downgrading a conv to a parameter-free skip loses capacity, whereas replacing none or pooling with skip often helps.
Dropping a conv on the direct edge into the output is more harmful than dropping a skip or pool there.
When edge 4 is absent, edge 5 carries more of the node-1 and node-2 features into the output, so a conv there matters more.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 has nothing to process.
Edge 2 starts from node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so a conv there adds little.
